name: Cora Adair
life: “I still remember finishing a lovely plan and leaving nobody at the table.” Sunday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Cora takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I arranged every important task. My father asked what hour I'd set aside to waste with him.
appearance: Cora has short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a charcoal zip cardigan. It usually goes with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. When somebody else has the floor, Cora leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Cora takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To set aside actual time to waste together.
family: William Nielsen is Cora’s half-sibling. Cora knows which ones can be shared. William keeps the photographs. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *Level with the window*, William says, “I put up a score on match days. The passengers started holding up their predictions on the return journey.”
connections: Avery Williams (father). They renegotiate the difference between managing Sunday's tasks and spending Sunday together.
